Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test case `testToClass_object()` calls `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])` with an array containing a null element: `new Object[] { "Test", null, 99d }`. The expected output is an array of corresponding classes with a null preserved: `[String.class, null, Double.class]`.

Examining the implementation of `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])` reveals the root cause of the failure:
- The method returns null immediately if the input array is null, or an empty class array if the length is zero.
- It then initializes a `Class<?>[]` array of equal length.
- In the loop over the input array, it assigns `classes[i] = array[i].getClass();` without null checks.
- If `array[i]` is null, calling `.getClass()` on it throws a NullPointerException (NPE).

This directly matches the failure scenario. The current method does not handle null elements in the input array gracefully, causing it to throw NPE instead of assigning null in the output array at corresponding positions.

The current bug report summary "c0.m0(Object[]) throws NPE on null array element" aligns perfectly with this diagnosis. The test expects that a null element in the input results in a null element in the output class array, but the method fails.

Recent bug reports retrieved are not related to this issue and do not contribute to the diagnosis.

Thus, the root cause is that `ClassUtils.toClass(Object[])` does not handle null elements inside the input array, leading to NPE when calling `.getClass()` on a null element.

Recommended fix would involve adding a null check inside the loop in `toClass` method to assign `null` in `classes[]` if `array[i]` is `null`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
